 | D58 | Real `---` YAML frontmatter for `.gram.md`, dual-read migration, threaded through lock + site nav | **A leading, `---`-delimited frontmatter block (`name:`/`lang:`, room for future keys) replaces the embedded fenced `` ```gramaire `` "General settings" block as the recommended way to declare a grammar's own metadata — chosen over extending the existing fence (the lower-migration-cost default a design debate recommended first) because the user explicitly wanted genuine frontmatter: free extensibility (lists/maps/quoting), standard tooling recognition (every markdown-aware editor/linter/static-site generator already special-cases a leading `---` block), and discoverability (metadata at byte offset 0, not buried in the Nth fence). Parsed by a new, deliberately minimal hand-rolled subset (`core/src/main/scala/gramaire/Frontmatter.scala`: flow scalars, quoted strings with backslash escapes, flow lists — no anchors, tags, multi-document, or block scalars) rather than a general YAML library, since `core` cross-builds to Scala.js (a JVM-only library like SnakeYAML can't) and the schema this project actually needs never exceeds this subset. `Frontmatter.strip` blanks the stripped lines to SAME-LENGTH space-padded text (not merely the same line count), so every downstream `SrcSpan`/diagnostic offset computed against the remaining document stays byte-for-byte correct with no caller-side adjustment. `Lr.scala` dual-reads for one release: a leading frontmatter block wins when present; otherwise the old fence still works, with a deprecation warning pointing at `gramaire fmt`. `gramaire fmt` gained a migration codemod (`GramaireCheck.migrateToFrontmatter`) that lifts `name:`/`lang:` out of the old fence into a new leading block and removes the fence (run once across every shipped example/grammar file in this same change). `Lock` gained an optional `name` field (populated from `Lr.nameOf`), following the exact omit-when-default provenance convention D56 established for `diagramView` — neither `checkStructure` nor `checkDrift` key on it. Sitewide, `parseMarkdownLite` (the one parser shared by the Notebook prose cell, Paper view, and PDF export) gained a frontmatter-skip step alongside its existing `<details>`/HTML-comment housekeeping skips, so the leading block never renders as a literal "--- name: X lang: Y ---" paragraph — this was the original, concretely-reported bug that motivated the whole change. `LabResponse` gained a `name` field (`Lr.nameOf`, read independent of whether the grammar notation parses) so the Notebook's download-source/download-PDF filename comes from the real frontmatter-aware name instead of a stale client-side `%name` regex that matched neither the old fence nor the new frontmatter format and always fell back to `"gramaire-notebook"`.** | Closes a concretely reported bug (frontmatter rendering as literal prose in Paper/PDF) and a design question ("how do I add real frontmatter, and how do the values reach the rest of the toolchain") in one pass, since fixing the render bug properly meant giving frontmatter a real parser and a real place in the pipeline rather than a narrow one-off text-skip. The dual-read window (one release, per this document's own migration-safety convention) means no `.gram.md` in the wild breaks the moment this ships; removing the old-fence fallback and its `knownSettingDirectives` machinery entirely is an explicit follow-up, not bundled here. Full YAML support was explicitly rejected as scope creep — the fixed, small schema Gramaire actually needs (`name`, `lang`, room to grow) never justifies anchors/tags/multi-document/block-scalar support, and a general library would break the Scala.js cross-build this project already depends on. |
 | D59 | A rule head's `NL` before `:` is optional — single-line, ANTLR/Bison-style rules now parse | **`Lexer.normalizeNewlines`/`normalizeNewlinesSpanned` now synthesize a zero-width head `NL` whenever a rule can legitimately start — right after a `;` (the previous rule's own terminator) or at the very start of the document — and the real one is missing, so `Foo : 'x' ;` parses identically to the traditional `Foo\n  : 'x' ;`. `Rule`'s own two productions in `bootstrapGrammar`/`grammar/Productions.gram.md` are untouched: the parser still only ever sees an `IDENT NL ':'` shape, real or synthesized, so every downstream production id in `CodegenScala.lrActionsScala` and `Lr.reduce`, every golden IR/DOT/`.g4` fixture, and `Productions.gram.md`'s own railroad diagrams and `.gram.lock` stay byte-for-byte unchanged. A `name:Sym` field (`IDENT ':' Sym`) is never mistaken for a head, because synthesis only fires at a position a field can never occupy — mid-`Body`, a field's `:` is never immediately preceded by a `;` or the document start.** | ANTLR handles single-line rules because it never reuses `:` for two jobs (`=`/`+=` bind element labels, `:` only ever separates a rule head); Gramaire reuses `:` for both a rule's own head and a `name:Sym` field, which is why the newline convention existed in the first place (fmt-output-contract.md's "Option A"). The mandatory trailing `;` already made "the token right after a `;`, or the document's first token" an unambiguous rule-start position (that's what let a prior revision drop the *boundary* NL between consecutive rules, D-numbered implicitly by that revision); this reuses the exact same boundary to also drop the *requirement* that a head's own `NL` be present in the source, without touching the grammar itself. Synthesizing in the lexer rather than adding new `Rule` alternatives was a deliberate choice: `Rule` is nonterminal #3 of the self-hosting bootstrap grammar, so any new alternative shifts every later production's global id, cascading through three independently hand-synchronized tables (`CodegenScala.lrActionsScala`, `Lr.reduce`, and every golden fixture keyed to the `lr` corpus) for no behavioral gain a lexer-level fix doesn't already deliver. |

When `declaredTokens` is non-empty, an ALL-CAPS reference that isn't among them is now a new, real diagnostic — `` undefined token class `X` `` — with a did-you-mean against the other declared tokens, mirroring the existing undefined-nonterminal check exactly. When `declaredTokens` is empty (the document has no `## Tokens` block at all — lexer-spec.md §6's whole-grammar "external mode", where the entire scanner is supplied out of band, e.g. `examples/readme.gram.md`'s `WORD`), an ALL-CAPS reference is left unchecked, exactly as before D60. Scoped to only fire when the document has actually declared something locally, rather than unconditionally, because `## Tokens` is genuinely optional (whole-grammar external mode) and a real, checked-in example (`readme.gram.md`) depends on that leniency. |
+| D61 | `Tokens.validateName`'s ALL-CAPS requirement stays a hard gate; round-trip fidelity is solved by `@spelling("...")` instead | **Investigated relaxing the ALL-CAPS-only requirement on a declared token's name to a lint (in response to a request to support importing non-ALL-CAPS names, e.g. ANTLR's `Digit` — ANTLR only requires an uppercase FIRST letter, not the whole word). Found it can't be relaxed in isolation: `Lr.classifyFenceContent`'s fence-role self-identification ("case is law", D-grammar-roles) requires *every* line in a `## Tokens` fence to independently look ALL-CAPS-before-`:` to be recognized as a Tokens fence at all; a lowercase-named line would silently fall through to `FenceKind.Rule` instead (and, post-D59, a single-line rule head is now `IDENT : ... ;`-shaped too — textually identical to a token definition line for a name that isn't ALL-CAPS).
